title: MPS in PyTorch 2.15
gist: Hugging Face's PyTorch team details PyTorch 2.15's MPS backend gains for Apple silicon: FP8 support, 5-6.5x faster MoE decoding (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 9.4 to 61.3 tok/s on M3 Ultra), 8x faster softmax, and a fix cutting Wan2.2 video VAE memory from 270 GiB to 8 GiB. The common thread is replacing Apple's MPSGraph with dedicated Metal kernels, with 2.16 moving attention fully to Metal.

themes.theme: MoE decode speedups on Apple silicon

insights.claim: In PyTorch 2.15, mixture-of-experts models decode 5-6.5x faster on MPS than in 2.14: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B rises from 9.4 to 61.3 tokens/s and LFM2.5-8B-A1B from 23.6 to 123.6 tokens/s on an M3 Ultra with torch.compile.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Sparse MoE models become practical for local inference on high-end Macs, strengthening the local-LLM use case for Apple hardware.
insights.quote: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B goes from 9.4 to 61.3 tokens/s on an M3 Ultra

insights.claim: The 2.14 grouped matmul on MPS copied group offsets to the CPU and looped over expert groups; 2.15's native Metal kernels read offsets directly on the GPU, removing GPU-CPU syncs that throttled MoE decoding.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: GPU-CPU synchronization, not raw compute, was the main bottleneck for MoE on Mac; software fixes unlocked large gains on existing hardware.

insights.claim: The dedicated small-group decoding kernel for grouped matmul alone yields about 1.3x more tokens per second for MoE models; the headline 5-6.5x gain combines it with fewer GPU-CPU syncs and faster top-k routing.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Headline speedups are a stack of several fixes; attribution matters when estimating future headroom.
insights.quote: MoE models generate about 1.3× more tokens per second

themes.theme: Dense LLM decode: GEMV and softmax kernels

insights.claim: Routing F.linear decode inputs ([1,1,hidden_size]) to GEMV matrix-vector kernels with fused bias gives a 1.23x geometric-mean speedup across 96 BF16 layer shapes from real models on MPS.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Modest per-layer gains compound across every token generated by every dense LLM on Mac.

insights.claim: The biggest GEMV wins come on small projections such as MoE gates, where the old MPSGraph path left most memory bandwidth unused, while large layers and LM heads were already near bandwidth-bound and stay near 1x.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Mac LLM decode is fundamentally memory-bandwidth-bound; remaining gains lie in small ops and overhead, not big matmuls.

insights.claim: Softmax over a 128,256-token vocabulary row in FP32 drops from 57 µs to 7 µs on MPS with dedicated Metal kernels, about 8x faster than MPSGraph, speeding token sampling for every LLM.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Sampling overhead per token shrinks materially for large-vocabulary models.
insights.quote: drops from 57 µs to 7 µs, about 8× faster than the MPSGraph version

insights.claim: Hugging Face's PyTorch team is systematically replacing Apple's MPSGraph with hand-written Metal kernels in the PyTorch MPS backend, using real Hub models to locate gaps and fixing them upstream.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Hugging Face is investing to make the Mac a first-class PyTorch target, a strategic bet on local/edge AI that also deepens its ecosystem influence.
insights.quote: more and more often by replacing MPSGraph with dedicated Metal kernels
insights.locator: A quick word about who we are

insights.claim: As recently as the start of 2026, running even small models on MPS often required working around unsupported operations, performance cliffs and unexpected memory growth.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Mac as an ML platform was immature very recently; the gap vs CUDA is closing quickly but from a low base.
insights.quote: At the start of 2026, running even small models on MPS often meant working around unsupported operations, performance cliffs and unexpected memory growth.
insights.locator: A quick word about who we are

insights.claim: Once a decode path contains no MPSGraph ops, PyTorch 2.16 can commit the command buffer every 16 kernels so the GPU starts while the CPU is still encoding, lifting compiled BF16 decode by 16% for LFM2.5-8B-A1B, 19% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 4% for Qwen3.8-27B.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Removing MPSGraph is a precondition for pipelining optimizations, so the migration has compounding second-order payoffs.

insights.claim: Already-landed 2.16 migrations include MSE loss (up to 12x faster on small inputs), std_mean/var_mean (up to 4x), and bincount, which on skewed data drops from 6.8 seconds to half a millisecond for 4 million integers.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: MPSGraph contained pathological performance cliffs; each migration can remove orders-of-magnitude slowdowns.
insights.quote: counting 4 million integers used to take 6.8 seconds and now takes half a millisecond

themes.theme: Memory and correctness fixes for generative media

insights.claim: Moving constant padding to Metal cuts total driver-memory peak for Wan2.2-TI2V-5B tiled VAE video decoding from about 270 GiB to 8.1 GiB, across 8,764 padding calls in a 28-tile decode.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Local video generation on Macs becomes feasible; hidden framework memory leaks, not model size, were the blocker.
insights.quote: peak driver memory drops from about 270 GiB to 8 GiB
insights.locator: A much smaller memory footprint for video decoding

insights.claim: On PyTorch 2.14 the Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE encoder silently corrupted images on MPS, breaking ComfyUI image-edit workflows; the 2.15 padding fix raises encode-decode PSNR from 10.06 dB to 29.95 dB, matching CPU.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Silent numerical bugs on non-CUDA backends are a real adoption risk for creative tools on Mac.
insights.quote: an encode-decode round trip now matches CPU at 29.95 dB PSNR, up from 10.06 dB

themes.theme: FP8 and platform roadmap on Mac

insights.claim: PyTorch 2.15 adds torch.float8_e4m3fn tensors on MPS at one byte per value (half of BF16) with F.scaled_mm supporting tensorwise and rowwise scaling.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: FP8 weights let larger models fit in Mac unified memory, narrowing a feature gap with CUDA.

insights.claim: In PyTorch 2.16, bundled shaders will target Metal 3.1 by default with Metal 4 only where needed, shrinking libtorch_cpu.dylib about 25% from 384 MiB to 287 MiB and laying groundwork for Metal 4.1 shaders with faster matmuls and native FP8 matrix multiplication.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Native FP8 matmul hardware support on Apple GPUs is the next step; current FP8 on MPS is mainly a storage win.

insights.claim: In PyTorch 2.16, scaled dot-product attention will run entirely on Metal; on an M5 Pro, GQA decode at 4K context drops from 465 µs to 65 µs and a 4K x 4K prefill with head dim 40 from 42 ms to 6 ms.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Attention, the remaining big MPSGraph dependency, gets ~7x faster on fallback shapes, further improving long-context local inference.
insights.quote: decoding with grouped-query attention (32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 80, 4K context) drops from 465 µs to 65 µs

insights.claim: MPS in PyTorch 2.15 requires macOS 15 or later and PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or later.
insights.speaker: Irakli Salia
insights.so_what: Older Macs/OS versions are being dropped, concentrating the backend on newer Apple software stacks.
